mainTopic: How the תוספת כתובה works like the main כתובה, a series of disputes between פומבדיתא and מתא מחסיא, and whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
overview: This amud opens by finishing a list of laws where the extra sum a husband adds to the כתובה (the תוספת) follows the same rules as the basic כתובה. The last item on the list, כתובת בנין דכרין, leads to a dispute between the scholars of פומבדיתא and the people of מתא מחסיא. The argument is over whether the sons can take that money from property their father sold. It depends on whether the משנה says 'they will inherit' or 'they will take,' and the הלכה follows פומבדיתא: they cannot. The same two groups then argue about whether a widow needs an oath when collecting from movables or land her husband set aside for her, and both times the הלכה is that no oath is needed. They also argue about witnesses told to write and deliver a gift document without a קנין. Here the הלכה follows מתא מחסיא: the witnesses must check with the giver first. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's opinion of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רב and רבי נתן argue over whether the הלכה follows him, and the גמרא suggests רבי נתן is the one who does, since he rules by אומדנא, a person's assumed intent.

steps.title: The rest of the list where the extra sum works like the main כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes listing the laws for which the תוספת כתובה is treated exactly like the basic כתובה. The list covers increased value, oaths, שביעית, a man who writes his property to his sons, collecting from poor land, a widow in her father's house, and כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The extra sum is like the main כתובה regarding: increased value; an oath; the Sabbatical Year; a man who writes all his property to his sons; collecting from land, and from the poorest land; 'as long as she is in her father's house'; and the כתובה clause for male sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list that began earlier. Each item is another law where the extra amount in the כתובה follows the same rule as the basic amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the list is that the תוספת is not a separate, weaker gift. It shares every rule of the basic כתובה. That includes oaths, being safe from cancellation in שביעית, collecting only from the lowest-quality land (זיבורית), and the sons' inheritance clause. The final item, כתובת בנין דכרין, becomes the topic of the next discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra amount a husband adds to the basic כתובה
An increase in the value of property
The Sabbatical Year, which cancels ordinary debts
The lowest grade of land
The כתובה clause giving male sons their mother's כתובה money as an extra inheritance

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'for increase in value', 'for an oath' and so on all continue the question raised earlier: for which laws is the extra sum treated like the main כתובה?

phrases.english: For increase in value; for an oath;
and for the Sabbatical Year;
and for one who writes all his property over to his sons;
to collect from land, and from the poorest-quality land;
and for 'as long as she is in her father's house';
phrases.notes: This is about the rights of a widow who goes back to live in her father's home.

phrases.english: and for the כתובה of male sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list that began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תוספת follows the basic כתובה for all of these laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra sum of the כתובה has the same legal status as the basic sum in every listed area.

steps.title: פומבדיתא: the sons cannot take back property the father sold
steps.stepSummary: A dispute is recorded about כתובת בנין דכרין. The scholars of פומבדיתא say the sons cannot take this money from property the father sold. Their reason is that the משנה uses the word 'they will inherit'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: regarding the כתובה of male sons, the scholars of פומבדיתא say it is not collected from sold, liened property, because the wording we learned is 'they will inherit'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute about the last item on the list, the sons' כתובה clause. This step gives the first opinion, from פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה wording 'יִרְתוּן' ('they will inherit') shows that the sons receive this money as an inheritance. Heirs only receive what their father owned when he died. So they cannot take back land he had already sold to buyers (משועבדים).

keyTerms.meaning: A major Babylonian yeshiva town; here, its scholars
Seizes from liened property that was sold to buyers
'They will inherit'

phrases.english: It was stated:
The כתובה of male sons:
The scholars of פומבדיתא say:
It is not seized from sold, liened property,
since we learned 'they will inherit.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the wording of the sons' clause as it appears in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר. כְּתוּבַּת בְּנִין דִּכְרִין, פּוּמְבְּדִיתָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the last item on the list and opens a new dispute about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתובת בנין דכרין is an inheritance, so it cannot be collected from property the father sold.

steps.title: מתא מחסיא: the sons can take back property the father sold
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of מתא מחסיא disagree. They hold that the sons can collect from sold property, because their version of the משנה reads 'they will take'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of מתא מחסיא say: it is seized from sold, liened property, because the wording we learned is 'they will take'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing opinion in the dispute. This side depends on a different wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the reading 'יִסְּבוּן' ('they will take'), the sons are not mere heirs. They are like creditors whose claim was set up in the כתובה before any sale. That earlier claim lets them take the land back from buyers. The whole disagreement comes down to one word in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A Babylonian town near Sura; here, its scholars
'They will take'

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a single word in the wording of a source can decide whether a right counts as an inheritance or as a debt.

phrases.english: The people of מתא מחסיא say:
It is seized from sold, liened property,
since we learned 'they will take.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with פומבדיתא by relying on a different wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתובת בנין דכרין works like a debt, so it can be collected from property the father sold.

steps.title: The הלכה follows פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the sons cannot collect from sold property, because the correct wording of the משנה is 'they will inherit'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: it is not seized from sold, liened property, since we learned 'they will inherit'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dispute and rules like the scholars of פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By accepting the wording 'יִרְתוּן', the גמרא defines כתובת בנין דכרין as an inheritance. So the sons can only collect from property the father still owned when he died. Buyers keep what they bought.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the halacha is': the final ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The sons' כתובה clause works like an inheritance ('יִרְתוּן'), not a debt. It cannot be collected from property the father sold.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: it is not seized from sold, liened property,
since we learned 'they will inherit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute between פומבדיתא and מתא מחסיא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows פומבדיתא: כתובת בנין דכרין is an inheritance and cannot be taken from sold property.

steps.title: Movable items set aside for the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If the husband set aside movable items for the כתובה and they still exist, everyone agrees she takes them without an oath. If they are gone, פומבדיתא says she collects without an oath and מתא מחסיא says she needs an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Movable items that are still there: no oath. If they are no longer there, פומבדיתא says: no oath. The people of מתא מחסיא say: with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between the same two groups. It starts with a case where everyone agrees, then shows where they split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the set-aside items are still there, it is obvious the husband meant them as her כתובה payment, so no oath is needed. When they are lost and she collects from other property, מתא מחסיא worries she may already have been paid, so they want an oath. פומבדיתא does not share that worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property (items that can be carried, not land)
They are still there, in their original state
They are no longer there as they were (lost or used up)
Without an oath

phrases.english: Movable items that are still there as they were —
phrases.notes: The case is a husband who set aside these items to pay his wife's כתובה.

phrases.english: she takes them without an oath.
If they are no longer there —
the scholars of פומבדיתא say: without an oath.
The people of מתא מחסיא say: with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another disagreement between the same two groups, after the one about כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the items exist, no oath. If they are gone, פומבדיתא says no oath and מתא מחסיא says an oath is needed.

steps.title: Ruling on lost movables: no oath
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows פומבדיתא: she collects without an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the set-aside items are gone, the widow does not need to swear before collecting. The worry raised by מתא מחסיא is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The final halachic ruling
A major Babylonian Torah center
The people of מתא מחסיא, another Babylonian Torah town

phrases.english: And the halacha is: without an oath.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A widow collecting after the set-aside movables are gone does not need an oath.

steps.title: Land set aside for the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If the husband set aside land and marked all four borders, everyone agrees she takes it without an oath. If he marked only one border, פומבדיתא says no oath and מתא מחסיא says she needs one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set aside land for her by all four of its borders: no oath. By one border: פומבדיתא says no oath. The people of מתא מחסיא say: with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The same pattern repeats with land. There is a clear case everyone agrees on, and a less clear case they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marking all four borders shows exactly which field is hers, so no oath is needed. Marking only one border is a weaker sign of what he meant, so מתא מחסיא asks for an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside (designated) for a specific purpose
Land, a field
Its borders

phrases.english: If he set aside land for her by its four borders —
she takes it without an oath.
If by only one border —
the scholars of פומבדיתא say: without an oath.
The people of מתא מחסיא say: with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same oath question to land instead of movables.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four borders marked means no oath. With one border, פומבדיתא says no oath and מתא מחסיא says an oath is needed.

steps.title: Ruling on land marked by one border: no oath
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה again follows פומבדיתא: no oath is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the land argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one marked border is enough. The widow takes the land without swearing.

keyTerms.meaning: By one border
With an oath

phrases.english: And the halacha is: without an oath.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Land set aside by even one border is collected without an oath.

steps.title: Witnesses told to write a gift document
steps.stepSummary: A man tells witnesses to write, sign and deliver a gift document. If they made a formal קנין from him, they need not ask him again. If not, פומבדיתא says they need not ask, and מתא מחסיא says they must.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he told witnesses, 'Write, sign and give it to him': if they made a קנין from him, they do not need to consult him. If they did not make a קנין, פומבדיתא says they do not need to consult him, and the people of מתא מחסיא say they do need to consult him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, a gift document. It follows the same pattern: an agreed case, then a disputed case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A formal קנין locks in the gift, so the giver can no longer change his mind and there is no reason to check. Without a קנין, מתא מחסיא worries he may still back out, so the witnesses must check with him before handing over the document.

keyTerms.meaning: To witnesses
Write and sign
Give it to him (the person receiving the gift)
They made a formal act of acquisition (קנין) from him

phrases.english: If he said to witnesses, 'Write, sign, and give it to him,'
phrases.notes: "It" is a gift document, and "him" is the person getting the gift.

phrases.english: if they made a קנין from him —
they do not need to consult him.
If they did not make a קנין from him —

phrases.aramaic: פּוּמְבְּדִיתָא אָמְרִי: לָא צְרִיךְ אִימְּלוֹכֵי בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: the scholars of פומבדיתא say: they do not need to consult him,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי מָתָא מַחְסֵיָא אָמְרִי: צְרִיךְ אִימְּלוֹכֵי בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: the people of מתא מחסיא say: they need to consult him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְעֵדִים כִּתְבוּ וְחִתְמוּ וְהַבוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another disagreement between the same two groups, now about a gift document instead of a כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a קנין, no need to consult the giver. Without a קנין, פומבדיתא says no need and מתא מחסיא says they must consult.

steps.title: Ruling on the gift: the witnesses must check again
steps.stepSummary: Here the הלכה follows מתא מחסיא: without a קנין, the witnesses must consult the giver first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: they need to consult him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the gift-document argument. This time it sides with מתא מחסיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here the rulings followed פומבדיתא, but in this case the הלכה goes the other way. If no קנין was made, the witnesses may not deliver the document until they confirm the giver still wants to give it.

keyTerms.meaning: To consult, to check with someone
It is necessary
It is not necessary

steps.whatToRemember: In this list, the הלכה follows פומבדיתא on בנין דכרין and on both oath cases (no oath), but follows מתא מחסיא on the gift document. Without a קנין, the witnesses must check with the giver.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume פומבדיתא always wins in this list. In the last case the הלכה follows מתא מחסיא.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: they need to consult him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement in step 9, this time siding with מתא מחסיא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without a קנין, witnesses told to write and deliver a gift document must check with the giver before delivering it.

steps.title: רב and רבי נתן disagree about following רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's opinion of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and reports that רב and רבי נתן argue over whether the הלכה follows him, without saying who holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the words of the משנה, 'רבי אלעזר בן עזריה etc.' It was reported that רב and רבי נתן disagreed. One said the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the other said it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It goes back to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in the משנה and reports a dispute between רב and רבי נתן about whether the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a woman collects the extra amount of the כתובה (the תוספת) only if she was already married. If her husband dies or divorces her after אירוסין alone, she gets only the basic amount, because he promised the extra money with the full marriage in mind. Here we learn that two אמוראים argue about whether to rule this way, but the גמרא does not say which one holds which view. That missing detail sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and one said. The two opinions are given without saying who said which.
The practical ruling follows this opinion.
The extra sum a husband adds on his own to the basic כתובה amount.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the first name (רב) goes with the first opinion. The phrase 'חד אמר... וחד אמר' means the גמרא is not telling us who said what. Working that out is the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, etc.
It was stated: Rav and Rabbi Natan,

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: one said: the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: and one said: the halakha does not follow Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר. רַב וְרַבִּי נָתָן, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It returns to the משנה after the earlier rulings about פומבדיתא and מתא מחסיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and רבי נתן argue over whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. This line does not say who holds which view; step 12 works that out.

steps.title: רבי נתן likely follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה because he rules based on assumed intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי נתן is the one who rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. Its evidence is that רבי נתן follows אומדנא, as shown by his ruling like רבי שמעון שזורי in the case of a dangerously ill man.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי נתן is the one who said the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. This is because we know רבי נתן goes by an assessment of what a person meant. As רבי נתן said, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case of a dangerously ill man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out which of the two holds which view. It argues that רבי נתן must be the one who follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and it brings another ruling of his as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's rule depends on judging the husband's unspoken intent: he promised the extra money only on the understanding that the marriage would be completed. רבי נתן is known to rule by this kind of judgment, because he follows רבי שמעון שזורי. In that case, a dangerously ill man says 'write a גט for my wife,' and we assume he also meant 'give it to her,' even though he never said so. Since both rulings rest on the same reasoning, the גמרא suggests רבי נתן is the one who sides with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be concluded. This introduces an attempt to work out an unknown detail.
An assessment of a person's intent: what he must have meant even though he did not say it.
A person who is dangerously ill.

steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows a common method in the גמרא: when we don't know who said what, we look at a person's other rulings to see what reasoning he usually follows.

phrases.english: It may be concluded that Rabbi Natan is the one

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: who said the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
since we have heard about Rabbi Natan
that he goes by an assessment of intent.
phrases.notes: Literally 'he goes after the estimate.' He judges what a person surely meant, even if it wasn't said out loud.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Natan said:
the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri regarding a dangerously ill person,
phrases.notes: This is the case where a very sick man says 'write a גט for my wife.' We assume he also meant for it to be given to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי נָתָן הוּא דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to fill in the detail left open in step 11: which אמורא holds which view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נתן is the one who rules like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case of a dangerously ill man. This shows he relies on אומדנא, the same reasoning behind רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
